links.outcome: Accuracy and response consistency of GPT-4o with vs without guideline retrieval grounding
links.effect: GPT-4o-RAG 83.5% vs GPT-4o 82.1% accuracy (p=0.12, not significant); consistency 97.3% vs 91.2-95.2% (p<0.001); lower variance.
links.quote: While the accuracy improvement of GPT-4o-RAG over GPT-4o was not statistically significant (p = 0.12), it exhibited significantly lower variance and higher response consistency (97.3% vs. 91.2-95.2%, p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Model performance on numerical/calculation questions and association of errors with numerical terms
links.effect: GPT-4o-RAG showed limited performance on numerical questions; TF-IDF analysis linked incorrect answers more frequently to numerical terms.
links.quote: GPT-4o-RAG outperformed other models in applied and clinical nutrition categories but showed limited performance on numerical questions.

unlisted_practices: TF-IDF word analysis of correctly versus incorrectly answered questions to characterize error patterns

screen.reason: The study directly evaluates the effect of adding retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to GPT-4o compared to baseline GPT-4o on a nutritionist exam benchmark, specifically assessing changes in accuracy, response consistency, and variance.
